title: Onboarding Evals Runbook: tooling, scripts, CI
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures practical implementation notes for onboarding new models into the applied-ml evals harness: recommended script primitives, dataset loader patterns, scoring functions, and CI wiring that have proven reliable for regression detection and repeatable evaluations. It is intended as a hands-on guide for engineers and ML scientists performing first-time model onboarding and for build/CI owners who need stable gating.

Scope and definitions:
- "Onboarding evals": lightweight to full-scale evaluation suites run when a new model (or new model version) is submitted for serving.
- "Prompt sets": curated prompts (golden + adversarial) used to detect regressions in behavior/quality.
- "Regression reports": human- and machine-readable summaries of metric deltas, per-prompt diffs, and flagged checks.
- Not cover: large-scale continuous monitoring pipelines (see product/optimize) — this focuses on pre-production gating.

High-level architecture recommendations:
- Keep the harness modular: runner (orchestrates batch runs), loaders (convert datasets to example objects), metrics (stateless scoring functions), reporters (JSON/CSV and HTML diffs), and persistence (artifact upload).
- Use an immutable run directory for each eval (timestamped), with: run.json (metadata), examples.jsonl (inputs + refs), outputs.jsonl (model outputs + timing), metrics.json (computed metrics), report.html (human diff).
- Persist artifacts to the central S3/GCS location and upload pointers into the artifact store (linked_artifacts).

Directory layout (recommended repo layout):
- evals/
  - runners/ (cli entrypoints, orchestration wrappers)
  - loaders/ (dataset-specific loader modules)
  - metrics/ (scoring functions, utils)
  - reporters/ (html, json, csv)
  - scripts/ (ad-hoc run wrappers for local dev)
  - ci/ (github actions, gating scripts)

CLI workflows and scripts:
- Primary dev CLI: evals run --model <model-ref> --promptset <name> --out-dir <dir> --shards 4 --seed 42
- Local smoke: scripts/smoke_onboard.sh — runs a tiny promptset (10 examples) with --timeout 30s and uploads only metrics. Good for quick validation before pushing PR.
- Bulk runs: scripts/submit_batch.py — splits promptset by shard count, submits parallel jobs to k8s job queue (or use the Dedicated pipeline), and waits with exponential backoff for completion.

Dataset loader patterns (functional, streaming friendly):
- Loader contract: loader.load(path_or_id) -> iterator[example_dict]. Each example_dict has keys: id, input, reference (optional), meta (free-form tags). Avoid materializing entire dataset in memory.
- Support two formats: JSONL (recommended) and manifest CSV with pointer columns (input_text, ref_text, prompt_variant).
- Use lightweight normalization step inside loader: truncate long inputs per model token limit, canonicalize whitespace, and optionally annotate expected function-calls for structured outputs.
- Seeded deterministic sharding: loader should accept seed + shard_index + num_shards to allow reproducible parallel runs.

Scoring functions and metric design:
- Keep metrics stateless and idempotent: metric.compute(example, outputs) -> scalar or dict. Implement standard interface to support vectorized postprocessing.
- Core metrics recommended: exact_match, token_f1 (span/QA), bleu, rouge_l, mrr, accuracy, calibrated_log_likelihood_delta (for probability-aware models).
- Behavioral checks: hallucination_flag (heuristic), safety_violation_flag (rule-based), and structured-output-schema-violation (for function-calling outputs). These return booleans and should be aggregated as rates.
- Per-prompt importance weights: prompt metadata may contain weight multipliers to upweight rare/critical prompts in aggregated scores. Document weight usage in run.json.

Regression detection and thresholds:
- Use baseline runs stored under releases/<model-name>/<version>/baseline-metrics.json. New-run metric deltas are compared against baseline with two signal types: continuous-valued metrics (delta percent) and boolean rates (delta absolute).
- Recommendation: a two-tier threshold system: soft-alert thresholds (e.g., -2% accuracy or +3% hallucination rate) for notifying the author; hard-gate thresholds (e.g., -5% accuracy or +7% hallucination) that fail CI. Keep thresholds per-promptset and documented in thresholds.yaml checked into repo.
- Highlight per-prompt regressions: show top N prompts with largest negative delta in the regression report with side-by-side diffs and model output tokens highlighted for quick debugging.

Reporting format and examples:
- Core JSON schema (flattened key/value): run_id, model_ref, promptset, created_at, metrics_summary (a JSON string in the content field of the artifact), top_regressions (list of example ids), artifact_paths (s3 pointers).
- HTML reporter: human-friendly diff viewer with colored token-level diffs, metadata column (prompt tags, expected behavior), and inline links to GitHub issues template prefilled with context.

CI wiring (GitHub Actions / gating):
- Small smoke check on PRs: runs scripts/smoke_onboard.sh — must pass within 5 minutes. Uploads metrics to artefact store and posts a short summary as a check.
- Full onboarding job (runs on merge to feature branch or when label `onboard-eval/run` is added): 1) checkout, 2) create run_id, 3) launch runner with shards=8, 4) wait and stream logs, 5) compute metrics and compare to baseline thresholds, 6) upload artifacts, 7) post summary comment with regression badge and attached report.
- Fail the workflow when any hard-gate threshold is triggered. For soft alerts, mark the check as neutral and tag owners.
- Use a small infra helper action (ci/eval-uploader) to sign and upload artifacts using the CI service account. Keys are rotated and stored in vault.

Performance and cost considerations:
- Default to small promptsets (100–500 examples) for gating; reserve larger stress tests for nightly pipelines.
- Use model-specific batching knobs in runner (batch_size, request_rate) and measure tokens/sec in outputs.jsonl for cost accounting.
- Cache completions for repeated runs (if promptset unchanged and model pinned) to save tokens during iteration. Cache keys should include model_hash and promptset_sha.

Debugging tips and common pitfalls:
- If outputs.jsonl is empty: check timeouts and model_ref mapping; inspect runner logs at debug level.
- Non-deterministic failures: ensure seed mapping is fixed across loader -> sampler -> runner. Document seed usage in run.json.
- Metric-skew from normalization differences: keep loader normalization code in repo (not ad-hoc notebooks) and version-lock it per run.

Example minimal-run command (copyable):
- evals run --model=registry/redwood/gptx-3.1 --promptset=onboard/small-qa --out-dir=./runs/onboard-2025-06-18 --shards=2 --seed=12345

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical location and minimal schema for per-prompt importance weights (repo-level thresholds.yaml vs per-prompt metadata).
- Integrate model fingerprinting: store exact model binary hash in run.json to avoid accidental mismatch between model_ref and execution artifact.
- Automate triage: create a bot that opens a draft PR with failing examples attached for author-driven triage.

Appendix: short checklist for a new model onboarding run:
- [ ] Create promptset folder with README, license, metadata.jsonl (example-level meta)
- [ ] Add promptset to registry and update promptset index
- [ ] Add or confirm baseline metrics entry (or mark as first-run)
- [ ] Run local smoke (scripts/smoke_onboard.sh) and verify metrics are sensible
- [ ] Create PR that triggers full onboarding job; monitor check and review report.html

If something here is unclear or you run into environment-specific errors, ping #eng-applied-ml with run_id and the s3 artifact pointer.

Author notes: this doc pulls together patterns we used for the 2024 onboarding wave (gptx onboarding) but tries to be pragmatic for smaller models too. Expect iterations as we integrate into the product-facing eval dashboards.
